_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with previously treated, unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive (IHC 3+) biliary tract cancer (BTC), as detected by an FDA-approved test; approved under accelerated approval based on ORR and DOR.

pivotal_trials.population: Adults with previously treated, unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive (IHC 3+) biliary tract cancer who received at least one prior gemcitabine-containing chemotherapy regimen; approval based on the 62 patients in Cohort 1 with HER2-amplified IHC 3+ tumors
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) by independent central review per RECIST v1.1
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 52% (95% CI 39, 65); complete response 2 (3.2%), partial response 30 (48%); median DOR 14.9 months (95% CI 7.4, NE)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%): diarrhea (50%, Grades 3 or 4 10%), infusion-related reaction (35%), abdominal pain (29%), fatigue (24%). Warnings include embryo-fetal toxicity, left ventricular dysfunction (LVEF decline >10% to <50% in 4.3% of 233 patients), infusion-related reactions, and diarrhea.
target_moa: Bispecific HER2-directed antibody that binds two extracellular sites on HER2; binding causes receptor internalization/downregulation and induces CDC, ADCC and ADCP, resulting in tumor growth inhibition and cell death.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — Exposure to ZIIHERA during pregnancy can cause embryo-fetal harm. Advise patients of the risk and need for effective contraception.

companion_dx_detail: VENTANA PATHWAY anti-HER-2/neu (4B5) Rabbit Monoclonal Primary Antibody (IHC) to select patients with HER2-positive (IHC 3+) tumors; approved concurrently with zanidatamab.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an Advisory Committee meeting or external consultants.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR), considered reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response [see *Clinical Studies* (14)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).

The review team considers the ORR and DOR results in Study 203 in patients with HER2 ISH-amplified IHC 3+ are reasonably likely to predict an effect on irreversible morbidity or mortality or other clinical benefit, and representative of a meaningful advantage over existing treatments for the proposed indication.

confirmatory_requirement.text: PMR 4732-1: complete ongoing randomized trial Study JZP598-302 comparing zanidatamab plus standard-of-care therapy vs standard-of-care alone in advanced HER2-positive (IHC3+) BTC (trial completion 03/2029).

citations.quote: 4732-1 Complete the ongoing randomized clinical trial, Study JZP598-302, entitled, "An Open-Label Randomized Trial of the Efficacy and Safety of Zanidatamab with Standard-of-Care Therapy Against Standard-of-Care Therapy Alone for Advanced HER2-Positive Biliary Tract Cancer", intended to verify and describe the clinical benefit of zanidatamab for patients with HER2-positive (IHC3+), unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer.

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy designation granted in 2020 for zanidatamab for the treatment of patients with HER2+ BTC.

citations.quote: Breakthrough designation for zanidatamab for the treatment of patients with HER2+ BTC was granted on 2020, and the data submitted to the BLA supports an accelerated approval in patients with HER2+ IHC3+ tumors.

summary.text: Zanidatamab-hrri received Breakthrough Therapy designation (2020) and Priority review, and was granted accelerated approval based on ORR and DOR from the single-arm Study 203/HERIZON-BTC-01, with a required confirmatory randomized trial (Study JZP598-302) to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: Breakthrough designation for zanidatamab for the treatment of patients with HER2+ BTC was granted on 2020, and the data submitted to the BLA supports an accelerated approval in patients with HER2+ IHC3+ tumors.

Taken together, the review team concluded that the ORR and DOR results in Study 203 provide evidence of zanidatamab's effectiveness and recommends accelerated approval as the conditions of 21 CFR Subpart H have been met.

requirement.text: 4732-1 Complete the ongoing randomized clinical trial, Study JZP598-302, entitled, "An Open-Label Randomized Trial of the Efficacy and Safety of Zanidatamab with Standard-of-Care Therapy Against Standard-of-Care Therapy Alone for Advanced HER2-Positive Biliary Tract Cancer", intended to verify and describe the clinical benefit of zanidatamab for patients with HER2-positive (IHC3+), unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer.

citations.quote: 4732-1 Complete the ongoing randomized clinical trial, Study JZP598-302, entitled, "An Open-Label Randomized Trial of the Efficacy and Safety of Zanidatamab with Standard-of-Care Therapy Against Standard-of-Care Therapy Alone for Advanced HER2-Positive Biliary Tract Cancer", intended to verify and describe the clinical benefit of zanidatamab for patients with HER2-positive (IHC3+), unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer. The trial should compare zanidatamab in combination with the standard of care in patients with HER2-positive (IHC3+), unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer.

requirement.text: 4732-2 Conduct an integrated analysis of clinical trial data to allow for further characterization of the clinical effects of zanidatamab, including pharmacokinetics (PK), efficacy and safety in the underrepresented racial and ethnic minority populations.

citations.quote: 4732-2 Conduct an integrated analysis of clinical trial data to allow for further characterization of the clinical effects of zanidatamab, including pharmacokinetics (PK), efficacy and safety in the underrepresented racial and ethnic minority populations. These clinical data, which may come from other ongoing trials with zanidatamab, should report an evaluation of comparative efficacy and safety between the aforementioned population and the population primarily represented in your trial.

requirement.text: 4732-3 Conduct an assessment of binding and neutralizing anti-zanidatamab antibody responses to evaluate the incidence of anti-drug antibodies (ADAs). Reanalyze the biliary tract cancer (BTC) samples from Study ZWI-ZW25-101 and all samples from Study ZWI-ZW25-203 using a validated assay.

citations.quote: 4732-3 Conduct an assessment of binding and neutralizing anti-zanidatamab antibody responses to evaluate the incidence of anti-drug antibodies (ADAs). Reanalyze the biliary tract cancer (BTC) samples from Study ZWI-ZW25-101 and all samples from Study ZWI-ZW25-203 using a validated assay capable of sensitively detecting ADA responses in the presence of zanidatamab levels that are expected to be present in the serum at the time of patient sampling. Reevaluate the immunogenicity of zanidatamab and the effect of ADAs on efficacy, pharmacokinetics (PKs), and safety of zanidatamab. Include the level of zanidatamab in each patient's test sample at each sampling point in the final report.

requirement.text: 4732-4 To implement a two-tiered reference standard (RS) system consisting of primary and working RS (PRS and WRS), prior to the depletion of the current RS, through the submission of a prior approval supplement (PAS) per 21 CFR 601.12.

citations.quote: 4732-4 To implement a two-tiered reference standard (RS) system consisting of primary and working RS (PRS and WRS), prior to the depletion of the current RS, through the submission of a prior approval supplement (PAS) per 21 CFR 601.12. requirement.text: 4732-5 To update the drug substance and drug product release and stability specifications for zanidatamab to include a validated C1q binding ELISA method with justified quantitative acceptance criteria, as a surrogate method to control the complement dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) activity.
